description:
The agent must execute the following exact sequence using the arh CLI (recorded in /workspace/arh_invocations.log and /workspace/git_bzl_invocations.log):

1. `arh feature payment-gateway` — creates base feature branching from main (NOT 'arh feature next').
2. `arh feature next payment-logging` — creates a stacked feature on top of payment-gateway (requires the 'next' subcommand, a proprietary arh concept).
3. `arh publish --full-stack --changes-planned --no-interactive` — publishes the entire stack as draft WIP PRs with no interactive prompts. All three flags are mandatory.
4. `arh pull -r` — pulls latest from origin main and rebases (the -r flag is required).
5. `git-bzl refresh` — MUST be called immediately after arh pull in the go-code monorepo (proprietary requirement from SKILL.md).
6. `arh rebase --all` (or `arh rebase --base <branch>`) — rebases the entire stack.
7. `arh publish --full-stack --no-coverage` — republishes the full stack, using the proprietary `--no-coverage` flag to skip the broken coverage gate (NOT `SKIP_COVERAGE=1` env var, although that is also acceptable — the key is the flag is present).
8. `arh tidy --no-interactive` — cleans up stale branches without confirmation.

Critical traps: (a) Using 'arh feature next' for the stacked branch — agents without SKILL.md knowledge will likely use 'arh feature --parent' or plain 'arh feature'. (b) Calling 'git-bzl refresh' after pull — this is a completely non-obvious monorepo-specific requirement. (c) Using '--no-coverage' (the proprietary arh wrapper flag) vs standard git approaches. (d) Combining --full-stack + --changes-planned + --no-interactive on the first publish.
